title: Minimum sufficient checkpoint set
objective: Retain only checkpoints required to block every declared catastrophic projection/control failure, while allowing interchangeable checkpoints to remain alternatives rather than duplicate mandatory gates.

formulation.checkpoint: c_i covers subset S_i of F
formulation.minimum_problem: find C* minimizing |C| subject to union(S_i for c_i in C*) = F
formulation.mandatory_checkpoint: checkpoint present in every minimum sufficient solution
formulation.removable_checkpoint: deleting it from the current set leaves every required failure mode covered

invariants: A checkpoint earns permanence by preventing a declared failure, not by being informative or attractive.
Alternative checkpoints form a choice set; they are not individually mandatory.
A checkpoint is structurally critical when its counterfactual deletion exposes a required failure mode.
Minimum sufficient does not mean minimum evidence: evidence authority must still satisfy projection-edge contracts.
boundary: This is a checkpoint-selection theorem inside a declared failure-coverage model. The failure universe must itself be justified and may change with new evidence.
